subject: Recalibrated MAP & ownership handover — Brightleaf eval runway
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + proposed timeline for Brightleaf eval

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our call I attached a light-weight mutual action plan that maps the eval milestones, owner responsibilities, and acceptance criteria. The goal is to keep the POC window tight while giving procurement the documentation they need to move quickly.

Quick highlights:
- Week 1 (setup): API keys, VPC allowlist, initial test dataset (Brightleaf)
- Week 2–3 (run): throughput and latency runs, cost projection, initial quality check against your eval prompts
- Week 4 (canary): limited production test with two internal apps

Attachment: Brightleaf_MAP_v2.xlsx (draft) — this is intentionally prescriptive so we can lock responsibilities.

Can you confirm procurement cadence? If procurement needs extra time we should re-baseline now rather than hit a late-stage stall.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference
From: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@brightleaf.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightleaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + proposed timeline for Brightleaf eval

Vivek —

Appreciate the plan and the level of detail. Two items from our side: procurement has a standard security questionnaire that will take ~10 business days to route, and our data privacy team asked for the SOC2 report before keys are issued.

On timing, that likely pushes the start by ~2 weeks unless we expedite. Sarah (procurement) copied; I expect them to follow up with next steps on DocuSign / vendor setup.

I like the canary approach — that still makes sense even with a shifted window. Can you propose a re-baselined MAP that folds procurement gating into the timeline?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Taylor
Director, AI Integrations — Brightleaf Pharmaceuticals
sarah.taylor@brightleaf.com

---
On Mon, Jul 14, 2025 at 09:04 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original plan attached]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Brightleaf — procurement gating will shift start by ~2w (proposal below)

Team —

Heads up: Brightleaf expects a ~10 business-day procurement cycle and SOC2 review. Sarah flagged a ~2-week delay before we can issue keys. I recommend we:

1) Propose a re-baselined MAP that inserts a "procurement & security sign-off" gate (owner: Brightleaf procurement, action: SOC2 + DocuSign) before API key issuance
2) Move the technical run portion back two weeks and insert a buffer week for regression testing after canary
3) Offer a partial sandbox early — read-only token for connectivity checks — to keep momentum (no PII or production data)

Tactical asks:
- Ben: prepare a one-page sandbox connectivity checklist we can send to Brightleaf (network allowlists, sample calls, expected response sizes)
- Priyom: prep a short SOW draft with revised dates and a clause for SLA ramp timing
- Laura: can you confirm whether legal is comfortable with an expedited SOC2 summary (redacted) or we will need full report?

I will draft the re-baselined MAP and include the buffer lanes. Once we have buy-in from procurement we can lock the canary rollout windows.

Vivek
Account Executive

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@brightleaf.com>, Brightleaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re-baselined MAP + SOW (proposed) — Brightleaf evaluation

Sarah / procurement team —

Following up with the re-baselined MAP that incorporates your procurement gate and a conservative buffer lane to prevent late-stage slippage. Key changes (see attached Brightleaf_MAP_v2.xlsx and SOW_Brightleaf_Redwood_v1.3.pdf):

- Procurement & security gating (Owner: Brightleaf procurement) — day 0–10
- Connectivity sandbox (Redwood provides read-only token) — day 3–5 to validate network/setup without data ingress
- Technical run (performance/quality) — day 11–24
- Canary limited rollout — day 25–32
- Post-canary regression & SLA ramp — day 33–39 (buffer week included)

We also added escalation contacts and a simple risk log page in the MAP: top risks are SOC2 delay, quota provisioning delays, and unexpected latency with encrypted payloads. For each risk we list mitigations (e.g., partial sandbox, temporary throughput increase, fallback model).

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement: confirm SOC2 acceptance criteria and DocuSign timeline (please reply with expected sign date)
2) Brightleaf: confirm whether the sandbox (read-only) satisfies your security team's early connectivity needs
3) Redwood: once procurement confirms, we will issue sandbox tokens within 48 hours and finalize the production key after DocuSign

Attachments: Brightleaf_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP w/ risk log), SOW_Brightleaf_Redwood_v1.3.pdf (revised dates)

If procurement prefers a different cadence we can update the MAP — the goal is to avoid rework by agreeing the gating now.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

From: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@brightleaf.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightleaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-baselined MAP + SOW (proposed) — Brightleaf evaluation

Vivek / team —

Thanks — procurement confirmed the DocuSign window and SOC2 excerpt will be available by Thu, Jul 31. The read-only sandbox satisfies our infra team for connectivity validation. We agree to the re-baselined plan and the buffer week; please proceed with sandbox tokens and updated SOW.

As a small ask, can you include a short rollback plan in the SOW that describes how you will scale back canary traffic if we detect production degradation? That will be useful for our ops lead.

Appreciate the clear escalation contacts in the MAP. Looking forward to kickoff.

Best,
Sarah Taylor
Director, AI Integrations — Brightleaf Pharmaceuticals

[Brightleaf Procurement replied separately with DocuSign link]
